title: Anyone here working on story-driven action-adventure games?
author: dnr424
selftext:
I see a lot of folks here working on RTS, RPGs, or pixel-art cozy games. Just curious, is anyone here developing story-driven action-adventure games?

Would love to hear what you're working on and how it's going!

comments.author: Baworistik
comments.body: I'm making a game where you fly through space, explore the sector and upgrade your ship. There's a story too - you find out what happened there and meet someone who's not exactly human. Planning to add combat later. Does that count?

replies.author: dnr424
replies.body: How do you ensure that the first 20 minutes of gameplay are engaging enough to hook players and make them want to keep playing? Do you specifically focus on this aspect during development, or does it come naturally as you build the game?

replies.author: Baworistik
replies.body: Actually, that was a big part of my thinking. I was trying to build a "path" where the player learns the basic mechanics of the game one by one, then the story starts, and only after that the real game begins, where the player (in my game, for example) is encouraged to upgrade the ship and discover more. But I'm not a pro, that's just my experience.

comments.author: Braunb8888
comments.body: I’m making an old school late 90s jrpg in the vein of Xenogears and Valkyrie profile, tons of combat, dialogue, world map, great music.

replies.author: Braunb8888
replies.body: Thanks man, I’m close to having a demo on steam. Gotta do some play tests and iron things out. I’m aiming for a ps1 feel

replies.author: Just-Routine967
replies.body: Is the dialogue AI written? It's the only thing that would put me off. Sounds awesome though, I'll be looking out for it.

replies.body: No I wrote the whole thing. I’ve had the GDD for 10 years.

replies.author: Entropydemic

comments.author: dank_summers
comments.body:
Doing a semi open world rpg. Have a demo built which is the 1st "level" of the game. It takes place in cave where all the walls are floors and you play as a cave monkey with a grappling hook. Combat is  momentum based so faster you are moving you do more damage 

Dialogue is light but the narrative and world drive everything that happening. Have the whole thing mostly done of how I want the story to go, but polishing this demo has taken me over a month at this point so slow process to make all the levels and get the progression right.

comments.author: whyaPapaya
comments.body: Yeah I'm actively making a story based rpg with two paths : one as an adventure RPG and one as an investigation style game.  Based on a DND homebrew world I've built. It's coming along well on both ends, today I was mostly updating the games music, and third act

comments.author: Ohgood9002
comments.body:
Im attempting to make a open world game like hulk ultimate destruction/prototype. Where the city is more of a sandbox to fight in than an interactive set like in GTA. 

The cities I can generate right now are already pretty good and lots of fun to traverse. I am doing a lot of detail work on them but the core city architecture is at a good spot. 

Traversal is feeling amazing. In fact I got traversal to feel so good that its what made me pivot towards a full action game. Movement consists of using this tool I call a gravity hook. It can switch between grappling hook and swing modes instantaneously. You can fire it off at your feet as well for a style of pole vaulting traversal too. I added in 6 (yes 6) double jumps. The first 3 jumps actually do stuff, the last 3 jumps are just for fun because you can do forward flips, side spins and backflips.

I also included the ability to grind edges and rails and wall running. When combined, the grappling, swinging, vaulting, grinding and wall running feel amazing and easy to pull off. Its alresdy so much fun to move around the landscape.

Combat is where I have hit a wall. I have no experience with action combat like you would find in Prototype or Hulk ultimate destruction. And things like cars that explode into pieces has been a struggle. I have taught myself some rudimentary 3d modeling and animation skills though.

I'll show it off soon. I just got access to fable so I wanted to focus on creating a npc generation tool with it to see if I can give npcs a face-lift.

That being said, I don't have any story planned yet, just gameplay and the environment. I wanted to see if I could get all the systems working before I dedicated time to a full story.

Buy really, the traversal feels so good that I feel the need to push through and figure out combat. Then I can worry about a story. 

Prototype was always a gameplay first type of game where no one cared about the story. So nailing down fun gameplay systems is my priority.
